guides.favoredWhen: Volibear wins by baiting Counter Strike and diving with the ultimate; Jax wins if E answers the full combo.

keyTips.text: Bait Counter Strike before committing Q plus W. His E dodges the full combo and reduces area damage, so feint first and engage into the spent shield.
keyTips.heading: Bait first

keyTips.text: Never commit into an active E. The shield plus stun reverses the exchange, so break off and re-engage after it expires.
keyTips.heading: Shield respect

keyTips.text: Dive with the ultimate once he is low. R disables the tower, so convert a won exchange into a kill instead of letting him turtle.
keyTips.heading: Dive finish

tips.text: Win short trades before his resistances stack. Your early bulk beats his pattern, so force the issue while the exchange still favors you.
tips.heading: Early press

tips.text: Punish his E expiry. The moment the shield falls is your engage window; step in as it ends rather than waiting for the next cycle.
tips.heading: Expiry punish

tips.text: Mark him with W, then decide. If the mark sticks, stay for the second hit; if he leaves the zone, take the won trade and reset.
tips.heading: Mark play

tips.text: Roam the tower line post-6 with R ready. The dive threat zones him off farm even uncast, so posture aggressively while it is up.
tips.heading: Dive threat

tips.text: All-in before his scaling answers you. His dueling grows past yours, so close the lane on your spike instead of farming it out.
tips.heading: Close early

tips.text: Chain Q plus W inside spent-E windows. The full combo with no shield to meet it is your kill condition at every stage.
tips.heading: Combo window

itemization.text: Consider Warden's Mail against repeated damage. The armor blunts his auto pattern while your combo pattern decides the lane.

sources.author: PH45
sources.rankClaim: Master (profile badge; no title claim) · Jax main

guides.favoredWhen: Volibear wins by stepping inside Q and timing R against the pull; Darius wins Q-edge spacing and Shojin stack conversion.

keyTips.text: Respect levels 1–2 and the bleed stacks. Take short contacts only; every extra auto feeds the passive that kills you.
keyTips.heading: Early respect

keyTips.text: Step inside his Q and time R against the pull. The inner ring denies his heal and stacks, and R answers the E he uses to catch you.
keyTips.heading: Q denial

keyTips.text: Make level 3 your all-in window. Q plus marked-W sustained trading is your strongest pattern, so force it before his items answer.
keyTips.heading: Level-3 turn

tips.text: Concede his level-1 punish. He zones the opening wave, so give the CS rather than feeding him the zone plus first blood.
tips.heading: Level-1 concede

tips.text: Step inside before the Q edge casts. Meet each Q windup by closing in, denying the heal and the outer-ring damage together.
Force the marked all-in. Land Q, stick for the marked W, and extend only while the mark pays out.
tips.heading: Mark commit

tips.text: Close before his Shojin spike. Once Spear of Shojin completes, his stacked trades outscale yours, so end the lane phase ahead.
tips.heading: Spike clock

tips.text: Hold R for his pull. The flip answers your escape, so spend R only after E is down or to answer the cast directly.
tips.heading: R discipline

tips.text: Fight before Sterak's plus Shojin stack up. Your window is the mid game; grouped fights late favor his resets over your dive.
tips.heading: Mid-game window

itemization.text: Respect his stacking with early armor and Warden's Mail value. Blunt the repeated damage while your Q-plus-W pattern decides the lane.

keyTips.text: Use Volibear's early dueling strength to pressure trades and look for a kill lead.
Level six adds a major duel and tower-dive option; use Stormbringer when the opponent is low and the dive is supported.
In late fights, use Stormbringer to get onto a backline target, then fall back to peel for allies.

tips.text: Keep the wave even or just on your side when not ahead; the longer lane helps run the opponent down and reduces gank exposure.
Use lane brush and Sky Splitter poke to make short trades safer before committing to a chase.
The first item component boosts his damage and durability enough to take more frequent duels.
Grievous Wounds reduces his healing and weakens his all-in and dive pattern, so respect enemy anti-heal timings.
Split push around side objectives and challenge the champion sent to stop you.
Avoid grouping when the side lane can pressure a nearby objective, but be ready to join when there is no objective to play toward.
At level nine the first ability is maxed, improving damage and dueling.
A second point in Stormbringer improves its damage and availability for team fights.
Group with the team and approach from the side or an unwarded brush to make the engage harder to answer.
Do not remain split away from the team late; opponents can force a fight while Volibear is missing.
Wait for Stormbringer before committing to a late fight; if it is down, delay and disengage.
Expect Volibear to shift into a frontline and peel role as the game goes longer, rather than relying on him to duel everyone.

itemization.text: Take Lethal Tempo, Triumph, Legend: Haste, and Last Stand with Demolish and Revitalize as the favored 16.21 page.
Build Dusk and Dawn, Plated Steelcaps, Navori Flickerblade, Spirit Visage, and Thornmail as the popular 16.21 order.
Start Doran's Ring, a Health Potion, and Stealth Ward.
Choose Randuin's Omen to replace Spirit Visage in the fourth slot when armor is needed against physical and critical-hit damage.
Max W, then Q, then E, taking Stormbringer at levels six, eleven, and sixteen.
